record.paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
record.original_question: What is the precise relationship between Pontryagin's maximum principle and dynamic programming for stochastic distributed parameter systems, especially in the presence of possibly nonsmooth value functions and the derivative information needed to connect the two theories?

evidence.quote: (11) The relationship between PMP and dynamic programming for SDPSs. PMP and dynamic programming serve as two of the most important tools in solving optimal control problems. Both of them provide some necessary conditions for optimal controls. There should exist a basic link between them. This link is established for finite dimensional stochastic control systems (e.g., [47]). A possible relationship unavoidably involves the derivatives of the value functions, which could be nonsmooth in even very simple cases (e.g., [5]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a controlled stochastic evolution equation in a separable Hilbert space H of the form

  dX(t) = (A X(t) + b(t, X(t), u(t))) dt + σ(t, X(t), u(t)) dW(t),  t ∈ [s, T],
  X(s) = x ∈ H,

where A generates a C₀-semigroup on H, W is a cylindrical Wiener process on a separable Hilbert space taking values relative to a complete filtered probability space, the control u takes values in a separable metric space U, and b, σ are suitably measurable coefficients ensuring existence and uniqueness of mild solutions. Associated with this state equation, consider the cost functional

  J(s, x; u(·)) = E[ ∫ₛᵀ f(t, X(t), u(t)) dt + h(X(T)) ],

and define the value function V(s, x) = inf_{u(·)} J(s, x; u(·)).

Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) provides a first- and second-order adjoint system whose solutions (p(·), P(·)) characterize optimal controls via a Hamiltonian maximum condition. Dynamic programming (DP) characterizes V as a (possibly viscosity) solution of an infinite-dimensional Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation.

Establish the precise pointwise relationships, along any optimal state-control pair (X*(·), u*(·)), between:

(i) the first-order adjoint process p(·) and the first-order spatial derivative (or first-order super/sub-jets) of V at (t, X*(t));
(ii) the second-order adjoint process P(·) and the second-order spatial derivative (or second-order super/sub-jets) of V at (t, X*(t));

in both the case where V is smooth and the case where V is merely continuous and possibly nonsmooth. Determine the appropriate notion of derivative (e.g. viscosity super-/subdifferentials, relaxed transposition solutions for operator-valued backward stochastic equations) needed to formulate this correspondence for infinite-dimensional stochastic distributed parameter systems with unbounded operator A.
artifact.category_tag: Stochastic optimal control in infinite dimensions
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work establishes correspondence relations between the maximum principle and dynamic programming for stochastic evolution equations in Hilbert spaces, covering both smooth and nonsmooth value functions via viscosity sub/superdifferentials and relaxed transposition solutions to operator-valued backward stochastic equations. Extensions to non-Markovian infinite-dimensional systems have appeared as recently as 2025. The Markovian smooth/nonsmooth case has thus been largely resolved in the literature, while fully general non-Markovian and degenerate distributed-parameter settings remain under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Relationships Between the Maximum Principle and Dynamic Programming for Infinite Dimensional Stochastic Control Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes relationships between PMP and DP for stochastic evolution equations in Hilbert spaces, both for smooth and nonsmooth value functions, using relaxed transposition solutions and nonsmooth analysis.
status_evidence.claim: The PMP–DP relationship for infinite-dimensional stochastic control with possibly nonsmooth value functions has been established in the Markovian case.

status_evidence.title: Relationships Between the Maximum Principle and Dynamic Programming for Infinite Dimensional Non-Markovian Stochastic Control Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Extends the PMP–DP correspondence to non-Markovian infinite-dimensional stochastic control systems.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research is extending the correspondence to non-Markovian infinite-dimensional settings, indicating the broader problem is only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Relationships between the maximum principle and dynamic programming for infinite dimensional stochastic control systems
status_evidence.snippet: Published version of the PMP–DP relationship for infinite-dimensional stochastic systems.
status_evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed publication confirms partial resolution of the problem in the Markovian Hilbert-space setting.
